runs.text: 1. What is type casting in Java?
Type casting is the process of converting data from one data type to another data type.
2. What are the two types of primitive type casting in Java?
Implicit type casting is also called
, while explicit type casting is also called
Implicit type casting is the automatic conversion of a value from a smaller data type to a larger compatible data type.
The conversion happens automatically, so an explicit cast is not required.
4. Why is implicit type casting called widening?
It is called widening because the value moves from a smaller data type to a larger compatible data type.
occupies 2 bytes, so the available storage space increases.
Explicit type casting is the conversion of a value from a larger data type to a smaller data type by explicitly specifying the target type.
The target type is written inside parentheses.
6. Why is explicit type casting called narrowing?
It is called narrowing because the value is converted from a larger data type to a smaller data type.
The available storage space becomes smaller during the conversion.
7. What is the main risk of explicit type casting?
When a value is converted from a larger data type to a smaller data type, the destination type may not be able to represent the original value correctly.
Data loss is possible, but it does not necessarily occur in every explicit conversion.
8. Does explicit type casting always cause data loss?
If the value can still be represented correctly by the smaller type, the conversion may not lose the value.
